title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Increasing
statement:
You have an integer array `nums`. A single operation picks any one element and adds 1 to it; you may do as many operations as you like, on any elements.

Return the fewest operations after which every element is strictly smaller than the element right after it (`nums[i] < nums[i + 1]` for every valid `i`). An array with only one element already counts as strictly increasing.
notes:
## Intuition

Operations only ever raise values, so the first element never needs to change: raising it would only force everything after it higher. Walking left to right, each element must end up at least one more than the final value of the element before it. If it already is, leave it alone; if not, raise it exactly to that minimum, because any extra height only makes the next element's job harder. Simulating the increments one by one also works but can take millions of steps; computing each gap directly is a single pass.

## Approach

1. Set `operations` to 0 and `previous` to `nums[0]`, the final value of the element just processed.
2. For each later index `i`, compute `needed = previous + 1`, the smallest value allowed there.
3. If `nums[i] < needed`, add the gap `needed - nums[i]` to `operations` and set `previous` to `needed`.
4. Otherwise `nums[i]` is already large enough; it becomes the new `previous`.
5. Return `operations`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 1, 1]`. Start with `previous = 1`, `operations = 0`.

- `i = 1`: `needed = 2`, `nums[1] = 1` is short by 1, so `operations = 1` and `previous = 2`.
- `i = 2`: `needed = 3`, `nums[2] = 1` is short by 2, so `operations = 3` and `previous = 3`.

The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass, constant work per element.
- Space: O(1): only two counters; the input is not modified.

## Pitfalls

- The array must be strictly increasing, so the target is `previous + 1`, not `previous`.
- Track the raised value in `previous`; comparing against the original `nums[i - 1]` undercounts after an earlier raise.
- Adding 1 per loop iteration is too slow for a long run of small values after a large one; add the whole gap at once.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `operations` | total increments made so far |
| `previous` | final value of the element before `i` |
| `i` | index of the element being fixed |
| `needed` | smallest value allowed at index `i` |

narration.2: No increments have been made yet.
narration.3: The first element never needs raising, so its value is the starting point.
narration.5: Fix the elements one at a time from left to right.
narration.6: This element must end up at least one more than the element before it.
narration.8: Raise it exactly to the minimum allowed value and pay for the gap.
narration.9: Its new value is now what the next element must beat.
narration.11: It is already large enough, so it stays as it is and becomes the bar for the next element.
narration.14: Every element is now strictly larger than the one before; return the total cost.
